# Priya Natarajan

I ran into Priya again this morning in the robotics lab while she was calibrating the new UR5 arm. She looked a bit tired but still had that focused energy she always carries. We've been working together more closely since she agreed to mentor my thesis project on adaptive grasping under uncertainty. It's been helpful having someone who's already a couple years ahead in the program.

## Context

Priya is a fourth-year PhD student in the robotics lab under Professor Chen. Her research focuses on human-robot collaboration, specifically how to make robots better at interpreting subtle nonverbal cues from human partners. She's originally from Chennai but has been in the US since her undergrad at MIT. She defended her proposal last spring and is now deep in the experimentation phase. I see her almost every day either in the lab or at the weekly lab meeting. She's become an unofficial mentor for several of the newer grad students, including me. Her desk is the one covered in sticky notes and half-finished 3D printed parts near the south window.

## Preferences

Priya strongly prefers getting feedback through Google Doc comments rather than tracked changes in Word or direct email replies. She mentioned once that the comment bubbles help her see everything in one place without losing context. She's also extremely careful about her peanut allergy, so we always double-check snacks for lab events. Last semester when we ordered catering for the demo day she reminded everyone twice about avoiding anything with nuts. She likes her coffee black with a tiny bit of cardamom when she can get it. In meetings she prefers structured agendas sent out at least a day in advance. She gets visibly frustrated with vague Slack messages that could have been an email.

## Interactions

Our interactions have mostly been positive and productive. Last week we spent three hours going over my latest experiment results. She caught several issues with my statistical analysis that I had completely missed. She's direct but kind with her criticism, which I appreciate. We also have a running joke about the broken coffee machine on the third floor that neither of us can seem to fix. Sometimes we grab lunch together at the food truck by the engineering quad when our schedules line up. She helped me prepare for my qualifying exam by doing two mock presentations with me. I still need to return that book I borrowed from her three months ago.

## Open loops

- Still owes Sam the copy of *Thinking in Systems* that she borrowed in October
- Need to schedule the next thesis check-in before the end of the month
- Promised to introduce me to her contact at Boston Dynamics who worked on similar grasping problems
- Her birthday is coming up on August 9, should probably organize a small lab celebration or at least get her a card
- Follow up on the peanut-free catering options for the March lab retreat she asked me to look into

She's been really generous with her time given how busy she is with her own research. I need to make sure I'm not taking advantage of that. The book return has been on my mind for weeks now. I keep forgetting to bring it in. Maybe I'll drop it off tomorrow along with some of those cardamom pods she likes. That might be a nice gesture before we dive deeper into the next phase of my project.

The more I work with her, the more I realize how much institutional knowledge she carries about how the lab actually runs versus how it's supposed to run. She's been a steady guide through all the confusing administrative parts of the PhD that no one really prepares you for. I'm lucky to have her as a mentor.
